When agents use this

When describing an effect, before a brief or motion ledger is built.

Skills: jig-mockup.

Names do not approve motion. The frequency gate and project decisions still apply.

Example: Circles around the edge

Before: A loose description could mean an event or selection.

After / recorded fix: Perimeter draw marks an event; halo marks selection.

Why: Naming the effect and linking its stage removes a guess before building.

Read the rules behind this example

From motion-vocabulary.md

Motion vocabulary

Use the person's description to find a name, then use that name in the brief and motion ledger. A name describes an effect; it does not approve its use. The frequency gate and the person's decisions still apply.

The coordinator answers a loose description with the exact term, a one-line meaning and its lab link before building. If two meanings fit, give the closest match and one alternative. If there is no stage, say so; agree a small lab comparison before implementation rather than inventing a link.

Our lab effects

These names describe the local motion study. The reverse-lookup method is adapted from animation-vocabulary; the meanings and limits below come from the person's motion decisions.

Loose descriptionExact termMeaningLab
Circles around the edge; draws a border after something happenedPerimeter drawOne outline traces the boundary to mark a real event, in its result colour; it never means selection.Perimeter draw
Glow around the selected thingHaloA steady outer highlight with a thin outline marks selection; it appears quickly without travelling.Halo
Looks alive while it works; slowly gets brighterBreathingA subtle 3–4 s brightness cycle reports real continuing work, stopping after about 30 s without events.Breathing
Scream at the user; keep asking for attentionAttention loopA blocking question breathes at about 0.9 s initially, then pulses about every 6 s until seen; interaction pauses it.Attention loop
A shooting star follows the connectionComet trailA bright head with a short fading tail traverses an edge once for a real transfer or focus event.Comet trail
The gap closes as the item disappearsFLIP collapseMeasure First and Last positions, Invert the difference, then Play transforms as the leaving item exits outside layout.FLIP collapse
Dashes run along the selected connectionEdge flowA directional crawl accompanies a static edge highlight while focused; the lab shows one finite pass.Edge flow
A dot carries a messageMessage dotOne dot travels source to receiver per real message; both ends retain their final facts.Single dot
Several messages travel quicklyMessage burstUp to five dots follow in quick succession; excess traffic becomes a count.Message bursts
Number rolls up or downNumber tickerDigits move in the direction of a real value change, with tabular figures keeping the surrounding layout stable.Number changes

Breathing and attention have an off switch, run only in view, stop when the tab is hidden, and become steady labelled cues under reduced motion. Attention stops on hover, focus or opening. Tune outline and halo strength per theme, light first. The lab is a demonstration, not evidence of acceptance in an application.

Common descriptions

Each row is paraphrased from animation-vocabulary. “No stage” means this toolbox has no dedicated demonstration yet.

Loose descriptionExact termMeaningLab
Appears gently; disappearsFade in / fade outOpacity changes while position stays fixed.State change
Comes in from the sideSlide inTranslation carries an object into view.Arrival
Grows into placeScale inAn object grows from nearly full size, usually while fading in.Panel open
Grows out of the buttonOrigin-aware animationScaling is anchored at the trigger rather than at the panel centre.Panel open
One replaces another in placeCrossfadeThe old surface fades away as its replacement becomes visible.No stage
One shape turns into anotherMorphThe outline itself changes shape continuously.No stage
The same object travels into a detail viewShared element transitionA recognisable object connects its old and new locations and sizes.No stage
Uncovers like a curtainReveal / clip-pathA moving clipping boundary exposes content without moving the content.No stage
Soft-edged curtainMaskA mask varies visibility, including partially transparent edges.No stage
Items arrive one after anotherStaggerSmall start offsets make a group readable as a sequence.No stage
First this, then thatOrchestrationRelated changes are timed as one meaningful gesture.No stage
Starts quickly, settles gentlyEase-outSpeed falls toward the destination.Easing comparison
Slow, quick, slow moveEase-in-outSpeed rises and falls during an on-screen move.No stage
Moves at an even speedLinearDistance changes uniformly with time.Easing comparison
Springy; carries a flick into the next moveSpring / momentumA physical response carries position and velocity toward a new target.Easing comparison
Bouncy when it appearsPop in / bounceAn entrance overshoots its resting size or position; visible overshoot is outside our house style.No stage
Can grab it while it is still movingInterruptible animationNew input redirects from the currently displayed value.No stage
Presses in under my fingerPress feedbackA small temporary scale change acknowledges pointer-down.Button recipe
A section folds awayAccordion / disclosureContent visibility changes while its trigger and expanded state remain clear.Fold
Resists at an edge, then returnsRubber-bandingIncreasing resistance communicates a drag boundary.No stage
Tiny jitter, broken movementJank / dropped framesMissed rendering deadlines interrupt continuous motion.No stage
Shiny loading sweep; floating backgroundShimmer / idle animationRepeating decorative motion; not used in the application toolbox.No stage
